---
title: "Measures of Central Tendency in Two-Way Contingency Tables"
author: "Anthony Morciglio"
date: "11/19/2025"
output: html_document
---

## Pre-amble

This R Markdown document simulates a two-way contingency table representing two categorical 
variables, *X* and *Y*.  
The goals are:

1. **Simulate a contingency table** using random integer counts.  
2. **Compute joint proportions**, **marginal distributions**, and **conditional proportions**.  
3. **Calculate expected values (mean), variance, and mode** for the marginal distributions.  
4. **Visualize the contingency table as a heatmap**,  
   and display marginal distributions using bar plots.

These steps illustrate how measures of central tendency can be computed using aggregated 
frequency data rather than raw numerical observations.

-----

```{r CT-Two-Tables, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)

# -----------------------------------------------------------
# 1. SIMULATE A TWO-WAY CONTINGENCY TABLE
# -----------------------------------------------------------

set.seed(123)

# Categories for X and Y
X_levels <- c("Low", "Medium", "High")
Y_levels <- c("A", "B", "C", "D")

# Generate random counts
counts <- matrix(sample(5:40, length(X_levels)*length(Y_levels), replace=TRUE),
                 nrow=length(X_levels), ncol=length(Y_levels),
                 dimnames=list(X_levels, Y_levels))

# Convert to data frame for tidy analysis
df <- as.data.frame(as.table(counts))
colnames(df) <- c("X", "Y", "Freq")

df

# -----------------------------------------------------------
# 2. COMPUTE JOINT, MARGINAL, AND CONDITIONAL PROBABILITIES
# -----------------------------------------------------------

total_n <- sum(df$Freq)

# Joint proportions P(X,Y)
df <- df %>%
  mutate(JointProp = Freq / total_n)

# Marginal distributions
marginal_X <- df %>%
  group_by(X) %>%
  summarise(MarginalX = sum(Freq) / total_n)

marginal_Y <- df %>%
  group_by(Y) %>%
  summarise(MarginalY = sum(Freq) / total_n)

# Conditional probabilities P(X | Y)
conditional_X_given_Y <- df %>%
  group_by(Y) %>%
  mutate(Cond_X_given_Y = Freq / sum(Freq))

# Conditional probabilities P(Y | X)
conditional_Y_given_X <- df %>%
  group_by(X) %>%
  mutate(Cond_Y_given_X = Freq / sum(Freq))


# -----------------------------------------------------------
# 3. MEASURES OF CENTRAL TENDENCY FOR MARGINAL DISTRIBUTIONS
# -----------------------------------------------------------

# Assign numeric values to categories for illustration
X_numeric <- c("Low"=1, "Medium"=2, "High"=3)
Y_numeric <- c("A"=1, "B"=2, "C"=3, "D"=4)

# Compute Expected Value (Mean)
mean_X <- sum(marginal_X$MarginalX * X_numeric[marginal_X$X])
mean_Y <- sum(marginal_Y$MarginalY * Y_numeric[marginal_Y$Y])

# Compute Variance
var_X <- sum(marginal_X$MarginalX * (X_numeric[marginal_X$X] - mean_X)^2)
var_Y <- sum(marginal_Y$MarginalY * (Y_numeric[marginal_Y$Y] - mean_Y)^2)

# Mode (category with largest marginal)
mode_X <- marginal_X$X[which.max(marginal_X$MarginalX)]
mode_Y <- marginal_Y$Y[which.max(marginal_Y$MarginalY)]

list(
  Mean_X = mean_X,
  Variance_X = var_X,
  Mode_X = mode_X,
  Mean_Y = mean_Y,
  Variance_Y = var_Y,
  Mode_Y = mode_Y
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------
# 4. VISUALIZATION SECTION
# -----------------------------------------------------------

# Heatmap of joint proportions
plot_heatmap <- ggplot(df, aes(X, Y, fill = JointProp)) +
  geom_tile(color="white") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low="white", high="blue") +
  labs(title="Heatmap of Joint Proportions",
       fill="P(X,Y)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

plot_heatmap

# Marginal distributions for X and Y
plot_marginal_X <- ggplot(marginal_X, aes(X, MarginalX)) +
  geom_col(fill="blue") +
  labs(title="Marginal Distribution of X",
       y="P(X)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

plot_marginal_Y <- ggplot(marginal_Y, aes(Y, MarginalY)) +
  geom_col(fill="red") +
  labs(title="Marginal Distribution of Y",
       y="P(Y)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

plot_marginal_X
plot_marginal_Y

# Display conditional probability examples
head(conditional_X_given_Y)
head(conditional_Y_given_X)

```
